statement: The default code-first generate/build/deploy pipeline emits the current handler-aware service-cell and Binding contract, supports at least two distributed operations and multiple HTTP handlers in one component, routes each call by immutable operation identity, generates per-handler least-authority policies, and keeps v1 artifacts invocable without a second runtime path. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: the v2 mechanism is landed (binding-schema-v3-handler-interfaces, handler-aware-runtime-invocation, service-cell-v2-generic-dispatch-world all SOLVED), but the CLI pipeline never passes multiOperationTarget (service-pipeline-command.js) so the default still emits the single-operation v1 world and no multi-operation example exists; this Quest is the default cutover plus legacy compatibility, not new mechanism work.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.

The service-source contract, entry generator, deployment-record generator, and CallCellInvoker remain the owners; this Quest flips the default target through them. No parallel compiler pipeline or second runtime invocation path.

The v2 path must be the live default of the public generate/build/deploy CLI, evidenced by a fresh code-first multi-operation service building and invoking through the default commands; a flag that leaves v1 as the live default is an unfinished cutover and cannot outlive the session.
Previously deployed v1 artifacts remain invocable with their existing invocation behavior on the same node; the cutover adds no second runtime path for them.

Cross-operation confusion, stale handler or operation IDs, and per-handler policy escalation must all fail closed; a service exposing two routes that call different operations plus a route authorized for only one is the passing shape.
